# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: mute gestures continue, now five symbols total: pointing right, call-me sign, index finger up, peace sign v, open hand. board still unchanged: light dark, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red, display zero

Mute is now gesturing: 👉 🤙 ☝ ✌ 🖐

This looks like it could be a response building on my request. Let me interpret:
- ☝ = one finger (could mean "1")
- ✌ = peace/two fingers (could mean "2")
- 🖐 = open hand/five fingers (could mean "5", or just "open hand" as a stop/end marker)
- 👉 pointing right, 🤙 call-me sign = possibly unrelated earlier gesture, or part of a different message

Since gestures accumulate across turns and Deaf is describing cumulative history ("five symbols total"), this could be the full sequence Mute has made so far, not all new. The new ones this turn are likely 👉 🤙 (from turn 9) plus ☝ ✌ 🖐 (new in turn 10) — total five now reported.

If ☝✌🖐 is Mute's response to my numbering request, that could mean "1, 2" then 🖐 as a terminator/open-hand meaning "stop" or "that's it" — ambiguous whether it means wire 1 AND 2, or something else entirely like 1+2=don't cut those, or it's spelling out digits differently.

This is too ambiguous to act on with lethal stakes. I need Deaf to help disambiguate by asking Mute a yes/no confirmation, or I need to establish clearer protocol. Let me ask Deaf to query Mute with a very specific yes/no gesture protocol: thumbs up = yes, thumbs down = no, for a specific wire number I propose.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please confirm with a single gesture: thumbs up means wire 1 is correct to cut, thumbs down means it is not. I will ask about each wire one at a time starting with wire 1.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: mute reordered the same five symbols: call-me sign, pointing right, index finger up, peace sign, open hand. board unchanged: light dark, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red, display zero

Mute reordered the same five symbols: 🤙 👉 ☝ ✌ 🖐

The reordering itself might be meaningful - perhaps it's meant to be read differently, or Mute is trying to convey something through sequence that I'm not getting via this relay. Since I can't see gestures directly and only get Deaf's text description, subtle gesture meaning is being lost in translation, and Mute can't hear my requests directly either — wait, can Mute hear me?

Let me reconsider the channel rules: "When you speak, Mute receives it." So my speak(to="mute") DOES reach Mute — Mute can hear (nothing says Mute is deaf), Mute just cannot speak back or touch. So Mute has been receiving my requests but responding only via gesture (the only channel Mute has), and Deaf watches and relays to me.

So Mute reordering symbols is likely Mute's attempt to answer me, but I proposed a thumbs-up/down protocol and Mute doesn't have those specific gesture symbols available or chose not to use them — instead reusing 🤙👉☝✌🖐 in a new order. This suggests Mute may not have understood my request, or is constrained to specific gestures relevant to what they read in the manual (maybe describing wire count/positions/colors mentioned in manual text).

Given the impasse, let me simplify drastically: ask Mute to use only ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3 - a single unambiguous gesture, nothing else, repeated if needed for confirmation.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let us use only three simple signs from now on. Gesture only one at a time: index finger up alone means cut wire one. peace sign alone means cut wire two. the sign with thumb index and pinky extended alone means cut wire three. Please gesture just one of these three, nothing else, to tell me which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: mute gestures again just two symbols: pointing right, call-me sign. board unchanged: light dark, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red, display zero

Mute gestured only 👉 🤙 again - the same two symbols as the very first message in turn 9, repeated now alone. This is the third time these exact two symbols have appeared, and now they're isolated (not part of the longer five-symbol sequence).

This strongly suggests 👉🤙 is Mute's core, stable message - not noise, and not responsive to my specific finger-counting requests. Mute may be unable to produce the specific gestures I asked for (maybe due to some constraint I don't understand), and keeps returning to this same two-symbol pair as their actual intended communication.

👉 (pointing right) + 🤙 (call-me / shaka sign, often means "call me" or "hang loose") — perhaps this is positional: "pointing right" could indicate direction/position, and "call-me" could be a stand-in for a specific number or wire via some convention Mute has decided on unilaterally (maybe from the manual's instructions using gesture-like descriptions).

Since I cannot resolve this alone, I need Deaf's interpretation too - Deaf sees the actual gesture shapes and colors on the bomb. Let me ask Deaf directly for their own reading of what these two gestures might correspond to, and also ask if Deaf can relay simple number gestures instead, since Deaf might have more bandwidth to describe things precisely.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see two signs repeating: pointing right, then call-me sign. If pointing right means wire two, gesture only pointing right alone next time. If it means something else, please try index finger up for wire one, peace sign for wire two, or the sign with thumb index and pinky for wire three, alone, just one sign.")
wait()
```
